subproblem.title: Inverse-function straightening of a C¹ function with nonzero differential (slice chart with h∘χ = first coordinate)
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m+1, h : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C¹, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open and w₀ ∈ Ω with Dh(w₀) ≠ 0. Then there are an open set B ⊆ ℝⁿ and a map χ : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ such that χ is C¹ on B, χ(B) is open, w₀ ∈ χ(B) ⊆ Ω, χ is Lipschitz on B, h(χ(y)) = y_0 for every y ∈ B, and |v − v′| ≤ |χ([t,v]) − χ([t,v′])| for all t ∈ ℝ and v, v′ ∈ ℝ^m with [t,v], [t,v′] ∈ B, where [t,v] := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)) = (t, v_0, …, v_{m−1}).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (h : Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ) (Ω : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (w₀ : Eucl (m + 1)), IsOpen Ω → w₀ ∈ Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 h → fderiv ℝ h w₀ ≠ 0 → ∃ (B : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (χ : Eucl (m + 1) → Eucl (m + 1)), IsOpen B ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 χ B ∧ IsOpen (χ '' B) ∧ w₀ ∈ χ '' B ∧ χ '' B ⊆ Ω ∧ (∃ Λ : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith Λ χ B) ∧ (∀ y ∈ B, h (χ y) = y 0) ∧ ∀ (t : ℝ) (v v' : Eucl m), (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)) ∈ B → (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v')) ∈ B → ‖v - v'‖ ≤ ‖χ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v))) - χ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v')))‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
This is step 2 of the parent proof (straightening at a regular point) together with the chart facts of step 3(a)–(b), for one point w₀. The output is stated abstractly: B is an open set (a ball here, instead of the parent's box) and χ the local inverse of Ψ := [h, π].

Notation: n := m+1, [t,v] := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons t (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v)).

1. (Coordinate map.) J : ℝ × ℝ^m → ℝⁿ, J(a,b) := [a,b], is continuous linear (check additivity and homogeneity coordinatewise with Fin.cases), injective (Fin.cons_inj, injectivity of EuclideanSpace.equiv), and J(a,b)_0 = a.
2. (Projection π.) ℓ := Dh(w₀) ≠ 0 is a nonzero linear functional on ℝⁿ, so K := ker ℓ has dimension m (Module.Dual.finrank_ker_add_one_of_ne_zero and finrank ℝⁿ = m+1). Let ι_K : K → ℝ^m be the linear isometry equivalence given by an orthonormal basis of K indexed by Fin m ((stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ K).reindex (finCongr _)).repr, and let P_K be the orthogonal projection onto K. Put π := ι_K ∘ P_K : ℝⁿ → ℝ^m (continuous linear). Then |π u| = |P_K u| ≤ |u| for all u (Submodule.norm_orthogonalProjectionOnto_apply_le), and if ℓ u = 0 and π u = 0, then u ∈ K, so P_K u = u and ι_K u = 0, hence u = 0. (This is the parent's π(w) = (⟨b_1,w⟩, …, ⟨b_m,w⟩) for an orthonormal basis (b_j) of ker Dh(w₀) = ∇h(w₀)^⊥.)
3. (The map Ψ.) Ψ(w) := J(h(w), π(w)) = [h(w), π(w)]. Ψ is C¹ (J and π are continuous linear, h is C¹), and HasFDerivAt Ψ (J ∘ (Dh(w₀), π)) w₀ by the chain rule. DΨ(w₀) is injective: if DΨ(w₀)u₁ = DΨ(w₀)u₂, injectivity of J gives ℓ(u₁ − u₂) = 0 and π(u₁ − u₂) = 0, so u₁ = u₂ by step 2. An injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional ℝⁿ is bijective; let e₀ : ℝⁿ ≃L[ℝ] ℝⁿ be the equivalence with (e₀ : ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ) = DΨ(w₀) (LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo, toContinuousLinearEquiv).
4. (Inverse function theorem.) ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph (Ψ is C¹ at w₀ with derivative e₀, 1 ≠ 0) gives an open partial homeomorphism Ψₗ with ⇑Ψₗ = Ψ and w₀ ∈ Ψₗ.source (mem_toOpenPartialHomeomorph_source). Put y₀ := Ψ(w₀) ∈ Ψₗ.target (map_source) and χ := Ψₗ.symm (a total function ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ). Then χ(y₀) = w₀ (left_inv). By OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm (Ψ has derivative e₀ at χ(y₀) = w₀ and is C¹ there), χ is C¹ at y₀. Being C¹ at a point is an open condition for finite order (ContDiffAt.eventually), so χ is C¹ at every point of a neighbourhood of y₀.
5. (Choice of radius.) The target is open, χ is continuous at y₀ (continuousAt_symm) with χ(y₀) = w₀ ∈ Ω and Ω is open. Together with step 4 this gives ε > 0 such that every y ∈ ball(y₀, ε) satisfies y ∈ Ψₗ.target, χ is C¹ at y, and χ(y) ∈ Ω. So χ is C¹ on the open ball(y₀, ε), and Dχ is continuous there (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). Hence |Dχ| ≤ Λ on the compact closedBall(y₀, ε/2) ⊆ ball(y₀, ε) for some Λ ≥ 0 (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn).
6. (The set B.) B := ball(y₀, ε/2). B is open and convex, and χ is C¹ on B. χ is differentiable on B with ‖Dχ‖ ≤ Λ, so by the mean value inequality (Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le) χ is Λ-Lipschitz on B.
7. (Image.) B ⊆ Ψₗ.target is open, so χ(B) = Ψₗ.symm '' B is open (OpenPartialHomeomorph.isOpen_image_symm_of_subset_target). w₀ = χ(y₀) ∈ χ(B) because y₀ ∈ B, and χ(B) ⊆ Ω by step 5.
8. (h∘χ = first coordinate.) For y ∈ B, y ∈ Ψₗ.target, so Ψ(χ(y)) = y (right_inv), i.e. J(h(χ y), π(χ y)) = y. Taking the 0-th coordinate (step 1) gives h(χ(y)) = y_0.
9. (Slice antilipschitz bound.) If [t,v] ∈ B, step 8 gives J(h(χ[t,v]), π(χ[t,v])) = [t,v] = J(t, v), so π(χ[t,v]) = v by injectivity of J. For [t,v], [t,v′] ∈ B, linearity of π and |π u| ≤ |u| give |v − v′| = |π(χ[t,v]) − π(χ[t,v′])| = |π(χ[t,v] − χ[t,v′])| ≤ |χ[t,v] − χ[t,v′]|.
Steps 6–9 give all conjuncts. The case m = 0 needs no change: K = 0 and ℝ^0 is a point. ∎
proof_key_steps: π := (isometry K ≅ ℝ^m) ∘ (orthogonal projection onto K = ker Dh(w₀)); |π u| ≤ |u| and ker Dh(w₀) ∩ ker π = 0.
Ψ := [h, π] is C¹ with injective, hence invertible, DΨ(w₀).
Inverse function theorem: Ψₗ with w₀ ∈ source; χ := Ψₗ.symm is C¹ at Ψ(w₀) (contDiffAt_symm), hence near it (ContDiffAt.eventually).
B := ball(Ψ(w₀), ε/2) with closure inside target ∩ {χ C¹} ∩ χ⁻¹Ω; compactness bounds Dχ; mean value inequality makes χ Lipschitz on B.
χ(B) is open (isOpen_image_symm_of_subset_target), contains w₀ and lies in Ω.
Ψ∘χ = id on B gives h∘χ = y_0 and π∘χ = tail, and |π| ≤ 1 gives the slice bound |v − v′| ≤ |χ[t,v] − χ[t,v′]|.

audit.reason: Projection onto ker Dh gives the required contraction and an invertible straightening derivative. The inverse function theorem, finite-order locality, compact derivative bound and mean-value inequality establish every chart property. The inverse identities prove the exact slice lower bound without additional hypotheses.
